note: Pre-registered before any probe was run. Prior evidence cited from research/experiments.jsonl and research/panel/*. Effect sizes are pooled Global WP unless stated.

cards.title: i1 is a second, unlabeled instrument stream: synthesize its labels with the target law and train on role-swapped sequences
cards.representation_change: The training unit becomes an instrument stream, not a sequence. Every sequence carries two book streams (i0, i1) but only one is labeled. If i1 shares i0's encoder and its quote path is decodable, the known target law (F = round(mean mid over next N quote events), loser -(sp+2m)) labels i1 for free; swapping the 52-column i0/i1 blocks gives a second labeled sequence per row group.
cards.mechanism: The regime is variance-limited (n_eff ~28 episodes per class-3 sequence; +0.0015..0.0034 per data doubling, E-152; valid-like data worth ~+0.003). New labeled streams of a related market reduce estimation variance.
assumptions_breakpoints: i1 uses the same per-side encoder as i0 (F8 suggests shared signed pairing 9/11)
i1 code grammar matches one of the four i0 tick dictionaries
i1 streams are not exact copies of other sequences' i0 streams (else zero new data)
law is exact enough for i1's class (exact for class 3; 86-99% loser for 0-2)
cards.predicted_observable: i1 price-code value sets / event rates match one i0 class per sequence class; i1 row states are rarely found among i0 row states of other sequences
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: per class, compare i1 vs i0 price-code value sets, event rates and spread-code grammar on ~150 valid sequences; hash i1 52-col states and look them up among i0 states of all sampled sequences
cards.falsifier: i1 values lie outside i0's code sets (different encoder) OR >50% of i1 states are found verbatim as i0 states of other sequences (duplicate data)
cards.cost: probe 20 min CPU; if supported, label synthesis 2-3 h CPU + 2 GPU-h fold-0/1 parent

cards.title: The per-sequence level/scale 'upper bounds' (0.727/0.719) are mostly in-sample overfit on ~28 effective episodes
cards.representation_change: Factor pooled WP into between-class, between-sequence and within-sequence covariance, with the episode (constant-y run) as the sampling unit. Cross-fit the per-sequence oracles on interleaved episode halves (and on temporal halves) instead of fitting and scoring on the same rows.
cards.mechanism: A per-sequence affine fitted on its own ~28 effective episodes absorbs noise at rate ~k/n_eff; that alone can produce +0.015..0.03 WP without any learnable latent.
assumptions_breakpoints: episodes defined as maximal constant-(t0,t1) runs approximate the information unit
OOS fold predictions are representative of the incumbent
cards.predicted_observable: interleaved-episode cross-fitted level oracle recovers < 30% of the in-sample gain; temporal-half cross-fit <= 0 (consistent with E-078)
cards.cheapest_test: CPU, cached ft_since s3/s4 OOS fold predictions + valid_targets: in-sample vs odd/even-episode vs first/second-half cross-fitted per-sequence level and scale oracles
cards.falsifier: interleaved cross-fitted per-sequence level or scale gain >= +0.008 (then a slow sequence-latent encoder is worth digging)

cards.title: Rank-Gauss clipping censors large queues, destroying far-from-move class-3 direction information
cards.representation_change: Treat volume codes as censored observations (clip at +-2.326 = Phi^-1(0.99)); replace censored queue size by an integrated depletion estimate (cumulative trade volume at that side since the code last left the clip).
cards.mechanism: Class 3 is a large-tick instrument with long queues; the queue race (Cont-de Larrard) is invisible while both best queues sit at the clip, which would explain 'coin-flip far from moves' (F4) as an encoding loss, not market efficiency.
assumptions_breakpoints: volume codes are global rank-Gauss with a 1%/99% clip (H-003)
the best-queue columns are among the saturated ones
cards.predicted_observable: >= 25% of class-3 rows have one or more best-side volume codes at the clip value, far more than in classes 0-2
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: per-class histogram of i0 volume codes at the clip boundary on sampled valid sequences, split by rows-since-last-i0-event
cards.falsifier: < 10% of class-3 volume codes at the clip, or no class contrast
cards.cost: 5 min CPU (shares the R01 data pass)

cards.title: Event-time multi-horizon auxiliary labels for classes 0-2
cards.representation_change: Re-express y as a fixed functional of the next N event-time mid increments (N=6/6/8 for classes 0-2) and supervise each increment (or the running mean after k events) as auxiliary heads, rather than only the next-move side (aux-next).
cards.mechanism: In class 3 the winner equals the first move side 99% of the time, so aux-next already carries the label. In classes 0-2 several moves matter; per-increment labels are lower noise than their rounded mean, so the trunk gets more signal per row.
assumptions_breakpoints: decoded mid paths available for classes 0-2
later increments are not pure martingale noise given x
cards.predicted_observable: in classes 0-2 the first-move side explains < 60% of |y|-weighted var(D); the OOS model residual correlates with move-2..N increments
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: from target changes at consecutive events in classes 0-2, measure share of D explained by the first event's target jump vs later jumps
cards.falsifier: first move explains >= 85% of weighted var(D) in classes 0-2, or residual vs later increments |corr| < 0.02
cards.cost: 40 min CPU; GPU 1 h if supported

cards.title: i1 is a different-tick instrument; decoding it with its own dictionary exposes a latent efficient price leading class-3 quotes
cards.representation_change: Identify i1's instrument per sequence class by matching its price-code grammar to the four i0 dictionaries; decode i1's mid in its own ticks; feed 'i1 mid displacement since last i0 quote move' (reset on i0 events).
cards.mechanism: Classic large-tick/small-tick lead-lag: a finer-tick related instrument reveals the efficient price that a large-tick quote reflects only at the end of a queue race. F5 found +0.14+-0.07 event-level lead in long stretches using the class-3 dictionary, which left 14-27% of i1 transitions unknown.
assumptions_breakpoints: i1 grammar differs from class-3 i0 grammar in class-3 sequences
the GRU cannot form the reset-on-i0-event integral itself
cards.predicted_observable: i1 event rate and code value set in class-3 sequences resemble a smaller-tick i0 class
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: same pass as R01 (i1 vs i0 code statistics by class)
cards.falsifier: i1 in class-3 sequences has the class-3 grammar (then F5 decoding stands, lead weak, E-088 i1_cross -0.0001)

cards.title: The public mask is softer than valid's (lambda ~0.02-0.05), so propensity^2 + true-mask FT under-serve low-propensity rows
cards.representation_change: Relax 'test mask = valid mask rule' into a one-parameter family m + lambda*(1-m); choose training weights (prop + lambda)^a instead of prop^2 with eps .03.
cards.mechanism: The LB-calibrated proxy fits best at lambda 0.05 (E-261, train-unlike lam0.05, LOO RMSE 0.0010). If lambda is real, rows with prop<0.01 (38.6% of required rows) hold ~14% of the public measure but ~0 training weight.
assumptions_breakpoints: lambda in the proxy is a real mask property, not a stand-in for a harder class mix
low-propensity rows are learnable
cards.predicted_observable: an LB probe zeroing (constant) predictions on prop<0.01 rows loses ~0.0075 if lambda=0.02, ~0.0022 if lambda=0
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: compute the incumbent's local loss from the constant-gate at lambda in {0, .02, .05} with an a3-threshold gate (causal, native-friendly); one LB upload discriminates
cards.cost: CPU 10 min + 1 upload; 2 GPU-h only after the probe

cards.title: Class-3 deficit is in magnitude (stop-out vs touch), which is volatility-clustered and predictable, not in direction
cards.representation_change: Factor class-3 y into direction (first move side) x branch magnitude (touch -1q vs stop-out -3q / +mq). Score how much of the model's weighted covariance deficit is magnitude vs direction.
cards.mechanism: Stop-out rows are 14% of rows but 43% of class-3 weight (E-160). Directions are near coin-flips far from moves, but move size may cluster in event time (volatility), which a row-clock GRU on wMSE learns slowly.
assumptions_breakpoints: branch identifiable from (t0,t1) lattice in class 3
magnitude has causal predictors beyond what the GRU tracks
cards.predicted_observable: >= 40% of the class-3 covariance deficit vs an oracle-branch readout is magnitude; a causal recent-volatility index explains residual |y| beyond |p|
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: class-3 scored rows, cached OOS preds: oracle-direction vs oracle-magnitude substitutions; residual of stop-out indicator on causal event-rate proxies
cards.falsifier: magnitude oracle adds < 25% of the direction oracle's gain, or residual |corr| < 0.02

cards.title: Competing-risks (survival) labels: time-to-move and side as a joint hazard target
cards.representation_change: From survival analysis: each row is an uncensored competing-risks observation (time to next i0 quote move, which side). Train a two-hazard auxiliary head with the survival likelihood; the direction readout comes from the hazard ratio.
cards.mechanism: Oracle next-event-time rescale is worth +0.015-0.017 (E-162) but causal hazard rescale <= 0, i.e. the model's magnitude/time representation is weak. A likelihood over event times uses far more label bits per row than the side label.
assumptions_breakpoints: the trunk's representation is the bottleneck, not the information
aux heads transfer to the wMSE head
cards.predicted_observable: time-to-move is causally predictable (rank corr > 0.3) and its prediction error interacts with direction accuracy
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: corr of OOS |p| with realized rows-to-move among class-3 scored rows vs a causal time-since proxy
cards.falsifier: OOS |p| already explains rows-to-move as well as the best causal proxy

cards.title: Selection tilt: the hidden mask is conditionally label-dependent, so E[y|x,scored] != E[y|x] and train rows need a non-causal selection weight
cards.representation_change: Invert the role of the mask: instead of a causal propensity p(x) (which cancels in the pointwise optimum), fit P(scored | x, future, y) on valid and use it as a training weight on TRAIN rows, so the optimum becomes the selection-conditional mean.
cards.mechanism: Propensity weights p(x) do not change E[w|y|y|x]/E[w|y||x]; only label/future-dependent selection does. True-mask FT moved the LB 3x more than predicted (E-144), consistent with a tilt.
assumptions_breakpoints: selection depends on y or future beyond x
cards.predicted_observable: within propensity bins, |y|-weighted calibration slope of y on OOS parent p differs between scored and unscored rows by >10%
cards.cheapest_test: CPU: cached OOS parent preds, propensity cache, valid targets/mask
cards.falsifier: slopes equal within 5% (E-103 already found labels add only +0.002 AUC)

cards.title: Tick-lattice readout: snap the D-part to the class quantum lattice via a calibrated branch posterior
cards.representation_change: Targets live on q*Z with t0+t1 = -sp on interior rows; apply the lattice operator (posterior over the few admissible (t0,t1) atoms given current sp) to the model's continuous output.
cards.mechanism: Discrete support could sharpen predictions when the model is confident near moves.
assumptions_breakpoints: model confidence near moves is under-expressed
cards.predicted_observable: post-hoc lattice readout beats identity on cross-fitted folds
cards.falsifier: prior evidence: post-hoc maps <= +0.0007, CE/atom heads failed (E-160, rejected list) -> expected to fail; listed for completeness, not probed

discarded_provocations.broadcast one prediction per quote-move: refuted by E-161/E-162: causal within-stretch smoothing -0.0003..-0.0375; within-run updates are information (2 rows before a move corr +0.91)
discarded_provocations.reconstruct global timeline / chain neig: forbidden by rules (no joining sequences); training-side chain context already covered by privileged teachers (rejected)
discarded_provocations.per-sequence scale/level from causal sum: tested as R02 (likely an overfit artefact); E-078/E-080 online recalibration with matured labels lost -0.015..-0.025
discarded_provocations.test class-mix reweighting / metric-awar: pointwise optimum is mix-invariant; per-class scale/weights rejected

post_hoc_cards.added_after: R01/R05 showed i1 is a distinct, slower instrument whose class-3 codes decode at ~79% with the train class-3 grammar
post_hoc_cards.title: Cross-instrument error-correction term and i0 level reversion (levels are invisible in shape codes)
post_hoc_cards.representation_change: Decode i0 and i1 mid paths in ticks; features ec_h = (mid1 - mid0) - EWMA_h, r1_h = mid1 - EWMA_h(mid1), r0_h = mid0 - EWMA_h(mid0) (restart at unknown i1 transitions). The GRU sees book-shape codes, not price levels, so level-relative signals need long signed integration it may not form.
post_hoc_cards.predicted_observable: partial corr with Dy given the GRU D >= 0.05 in long quiet stretches, and a cross-fitted linear D-correction lifts pooled WP
post_hoc_cards.falsifier: leave-one-fold-out linear D-correction on class-3 rows gives pooled delta < +0.0003 or folds disagree

post_hoc_cards.added_after: R03 showed volume codes are uncensored snapshots; targets change only on i0 price-code rows
post_hoc_cards.title: Event-preserving row thinning is an exact label symmetry; use it as training augmentation
post_hoc_cards.representation_change: Treat the row clock as a nuisance: dropping rows without an i0 price-code change leaves every kept row's target unchanged (targets live on the quote clock, features are snapshots). Random thinning yields new, exactly labelled training sequences.
post_hoc_cards.mechanism: Training is memorization-limited (12 epochs peak at 5 then -0.027, E-153; data doubling +0.0015..0.0034). An exact symmetry gives fresh views of the same episodes and allows more epochs.
post_hoc_cards.predicted_observable: CPU: on fold-0 OOS members, thinning 30% of droppable rows keeps kept-row WP within 0.002 while corr(pA, pB) < 0.995 (density-sensitive without signal) -> augmentation plausible; WP drop > 0.005 -> density carries signal, reject
post_hoc_cards.falsifier: kept-row WP drops > 0.005 under thinning, or corr(pA, pB) > 0.998 (already invariant, augmentation adds nothing)
post_hoc_cards.cost: CPU 25 min; GPU 2 h if supported
